title: The confirmation page offers only "Return to your dashboard"; Design release 1 also offers "Create a new notification"

finding.frontend: Under "How to view or amend this notification" the confirmation page carries one link, "Return to your dashboard" (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/confirmation/template.njk:23-27, wording at src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/confirmation/copy/copy.en.js:19-23). A trader who has just submitted one consignment and has another to notify has to go back to the dashboard and find the start button there.
finding.prototype: Design release 1 offers two links in the same block: "Return to your dashboard" and, below it, "Create a new notification" pointing straight at the start of the journey (app/views/notification-submitted.html:49-59).
finding.difference: Add a "Create a new notification" link below "Return to your dashboard" on the confirmation page, pointing at the same route the dashboard's start action uses. This is a template and copy change in the confirmation feature; the route already exists.
finding.falsifiedBy: Finding a second link in the "How to view or amend this notification" block on fe-confirmation. The captured DOM has exactly one anchor there, to the dashboard.
finding.verification: Ran the falsifier by looking, not just grepping: evidence/frontend@76a864ba/page/fe-confirmation.png shows "Return to your dashboard" alone under that heading, and evidence/prototype@491b3926/page/dr1-notification-submitted.png shows "Return to your dashboard" with "Create a new notification" below it. The citation is exact — app/views/notification-submitted.html:50-59 is the whole section, with the two anchors at :54 and :57, the second pointing at /create-notification. Checked the one thing that could have made this a false positive, that Create a new notification might be a placeholder href the contract excludes: it is not, it points at the start of the journey, and the contract's placeholder exclusion covers # hrefs only. Also checked the neighbouring sentence, which differs too — the frontend says "You can view or amend this notification from your dashboard and resubmit it" where Design release 1 says "You can view or change this notification from your dashboard" — and deliberately did not raise it: the extra words describe the frontend's amend-and-resubmit journey, which Design release 1 does not have, so it falls under the one-sided-feature rule already recorded in review--deleting-and-cancelling-an-amendment-are-one-sided. CORRECT.
